all_completion_and_external_effects_reso.mechanism: every hash column is a checked sha256 domain rather than free text, an eviction records when and why, a rolled-back or failed seal leaves nothing behind, and an evicted archive row stays in place as evidence rather than being deleted

governing_schemas_authority_boundaries_f.mechanism: the assertions are PostgreSQL's own catalog answers after the migration ran: the nine tables, the seven NOT NULL checkpoint bindings, the sha256 and identifier domains under deterministic C collation, the five append-only and evaluator guards, and the two SECURITY DEFINER entry points

happy_negative_crash_resume_adversarial_.mechanism: lineage resolves to its root, islands specialise, the archive keeps whole niches, and a checkpoint seals in one statement; every attack is executed as the runtime principal against the real server, including a rolled-back seal that must leave no resume point at all

no_candidate_model_prompt_backend_or_hoo.mechanism: a checkpoint may bind only the evaluator its run was opened with, so a resume point cannot swap the evaluator (EF4-I43); a run row cannot be rewritten; and a protected archive entry cannot be evicted for low fitness through the function, a direct UPDATE, or a DELETE the runtime does not hold (EF4-I49)
